title: DDL_LOCK_TIMEOUT set to the maximum outlives any maintenance window
expected_feedback: Standard: 1000000 seconds is Oracle's ceiling — about 11.5 days. The DDL will not fail; it will sit in the lock queue long past the end of any maintenance window, and every DML that arrives behind it queues too, so a migration that looks stalled is actually taking the application down by degrees. The value should be sized to the window, not to the maximum the parameter accepts. Pick something a human would wait for (3–10s for OLTP, up to a minute or two inside an exclusive window) so that failure is fast, visible, and retryable.
violated_rule: DDL_LOCK_TIMEOUT set before every DDL session
